overview.headline: How absorbed carbon dioxide makes seawater more acidic and harms shell building organisms

keyPoints.point: Ocean acidification is a long term reduction in ocean pH driven by carbon dioxide uptake.
keyPoints.quote: a reduction in the pH of the ocean over an extended period of time, caused primarily by uptake of carbon dioxide

keyPoints.point: The ocean absorbs about 30 percent of carbon dioxide released to the atmosphere.
keyPoints.quote: The ocean absorbs about 30 percent of the CO2 that is released in the atmosphere

keyPoints.point: Absorbed carbon dioxide raises hydrogen ion concentration and makes seawater more acidic while carbonate ions become less abundant.
keyPoints.quote: This increase causes the seawater to become more acidic and causes carbonate ions to be relatively less abundant.

keyPoints.point: Decreases in carbonate ions make it difficult for calcifying organisms such as oysters to build shells.
keyPoints.quote: Decreases in carbonate ions can make building and maintaining shells and other calcium carbonate structures difficult for calcifying organisms

keyTerms.gloss: reduction in ocean pH over extended time caused by carbon dioxide uptake
keyTerms.quote: Ocean acidification refers to a reduction in the pH of the ocean

keyTerms.gloss: gas whose atmospheric concentration has increased due to fossil fuel burning
keyTerms.quote: the concentration of carbon dioxide (CO2) in the atmosphere has increased

keyTerms.gloss: building blocks for shells and coral skeletons that become relatively less abundant in acidic water
keyTerms.quote: causes carbonate ions to be relatively less abundant

keyTerms.gloss: particles whose increased concentration makes seawater more acidic
organisms such as oysters and corals that build calcium carbonate shells
keyTerms.quote: difficult for calcifying organisms such as oysters, clams, sea urchins
